chunks: Sa‘d narrated from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas‘adah ibn Sadaqah al-Raba‘i, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked: Is it suitable for the place of a latrine to be made into a masjid? He said: If enough soil is cast over it to cover that, or to cut off its odor, then there is no harm. That is because the soil purifies it; with this the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has passed.

key_terms.التُّرَابِ: soil or earth used here as a purifying covering
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition), indicating established transmitted practice
key_terms.مَسْجِدًا: a place of sajdah; here, a masjid used for worship

ai.seo_question: Can a former latrine site be used as a masjid if it is covered with soil?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding transforming a former place of filth into a masjid. It states that if soil is placed over it sufficiently to conceal it or remove its odor, there is no objection, because soil serves as a means of purification according to the sunnah (prophetic tradition).
